headline: Flying Machine Soars Three Miles In Teeth Of High Wind
dateline: KILL DEVIL HILLS, NORTH CAROLINA, 17 DECEMBER 1903
summary: Orville Wright flew a powered heavier-than-air machine for twelve seconds over one hundred and twenty feet of sand at Kill Devil Hills on the morning of 17 December 1903, the first of four flights made that day.
body: The brothers laid a sixty-foot wooden launching rail on level sand and waited out a north wind gusting to twenty-seven miles an hour. At about half past ten Orville lay prone at the hip cradle and released the restraining wire. The machine lifted from the rail and flew one hundred and twenty feet in twelve seconds, Wilbur running alongside at the wingtip. John T. Daniels of the Kill Devil Hills life-saving station squeezed the shutter of a camera the brothers had aimed at the end of the rail, making the only photograph of the moment. Three further flights followed, the last covering eight hundred and fifty-two feet in fifty-nine seconds. A gust later overturned the machine on the sand and damaged it beyond flying that season.
context: The flights closed four seasons of work at Kitty Hawk, chosen for its steady wind and soft sand. The brothers had built their own wind tunnel to correct published lift tables, settled on wing-warping and a movable rudder for control, and had their machinist Charlie Taylor build a twelve-horsepower engine when no manufacturer would supply one light enough.

world.subject: A long wooden launching rail on wind-packed sand at Kill Devil Hills on a cold December morning, a canvas-winged biplane machine resting on it, two men in dark overcoats and a camera on a wooden tripod standing by.

anchors.position: at the end of the rail

world.environment: Wind-packed grey sand printed with footprints and skid marks, dry grass bending in a steady north wind, an overcast winter sky.
world.style: Glass-plate photography of 1903, monochrome, soft grain, flat overcast light.
world.idle: The men stand steady beside the rail with their coat tails and cap brims flicking in the wind, breath clouding faintly, while the canvas of the wings trembles and the bracing wires hum against the gusts.
world.travel: Packed sand and skid marks slide past underfoot along the line of the wooden rail, blown grains streaking low across the ground as dry grass rakes past at the edges.
guards: the machine rests on its skids on the rail, its propellers behind the wings — a pusher arrangement, not a nose propeller

events.name: Engine and chains
events.detail: The engine on the lower wing shakes into life and settles into a rough beat, the two chain drives clattering as the pusher propellers behind the wings spin up into a blur and blown sand skitters away beneath the machine.

events.name: Release the restraining wire
events.detail: The restraining wire at the rail springs loose and whips aside, the machine slides forward along the wooden rail with the near man running at the wingtip, then lifts a few feet clear of the sand and holds there against the wind.

events.name: The shutter
events.detail: The man at the tripod on the right squeezes the shutter bulb, the camera on its wooden legs shifting slightly in the wind as the plate is exposed, and he lowers his hand again.

vertical.jump: The viewpoint rises sharply off the packed sand, clearing the height of the rail for a moment before dropping back down to the ground.
vertical.crouch: The camera lowers toward the ground as the viewpoint crouches down low beside the wooden rail, close to the sand and the skid marks.
vertical.stand: The viewpoint straightens back up out of the crouch.
